title: Check Point Harmony SASE Private Access (Check Point)

Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.

dataSources: `sourcetype=cp_log` (VPN/access logs) Indexes: zt. Sourcetypes: cp_log. Key fields: dst, fail_pct, ok, rule_name, src_user_name. Validate field extraction in Search before saving the alert; compare event counts to the vendor admin console.
spl:
index=zt sourcetype="cp_log" product="VPN" earliest=-24h
| eval ok=if(match(lower(action),"(?i)accept|allow") AND isnotnull(rule_name),1,0)
| stats count sum(ok) as successes by src_user_name, dst, rule_name
| eval fail_pct=round(100*(count-successes)/count,1)
| where fail_pct > 5
| sort -fail_pct
description: Harmony SASE Private Access (ZTNA) grants per-application access to private resources without VPN. Connector health, access decisions, and latency determine user experience for internal applications.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Check Point Harmony SASE Private Access (ZTNA) events in `index=checkpoint` with `sourcetype=checkpoint:harmony`. Key fields: `action` (Accept/Drop), `rule_name`, `user`, `src`, `dst` (private app IP), `service`, `application_name`, `auth_method`.
• Harmony SASE Private Access = ZTNA for accessing internal applications. Users connect through the Harmony Connect client, which establishes a zero-trust tunnel to the private app. Access decisions are based on identity, device posture, and granular rules.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Verify private access events:
```spl
index=checkpoint sourcetype="checkpoint:harmony" earliest=-24h
| where isnotnull(application_name) AND match(dst, "^(10\\.|172\\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-1])\\.|192\\.168\\.)")
| stats count by action, application_name
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — Private access overview:
```spl
index=checkpoint sourcetype="checkpoint:harmony" earliest=-24h
| where match(dst, "^(10\\.|172\\.|192\\.168\\.)")
| stats count(eval(action="Accept")) as accepted count(eval(action="Drop")) as denied dc(user) as users by application_name, rule_name
| eval deny_rate=round(denied/(accepted+denied)*100, 1)
| sort - deny_rate
```

Understanding this SPL: Tracks private application access success/deny rates through Harmony SASE. High deny rates mean users fail ZTNA policy checks (wrong group, non-compliant device). The `rule_name` shows which policy is responsible.

Denied access analysis:
```spl
index=checkpoint sourcetype="checkpoint:harmony" action=Drop earliest=-24h
| where match(dst, "^(10\\.|172\\.|192\\.168\\.)")
| stats count by user, application_name, rule_name
| sort - count
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) Access a private app via Harmony Connect. Verify accept event.
(b) Attempt access without proper device posture. Verify deny.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard: Row 1 — App access rates. Row 2 — Denied users. Row 3 — Rule match distribution.
Alert: When deny rate exceeds 15% for critical private apps.

Runbook:
1. **High deny rate** — Check device posture requirements. May be too strict.
2. **User in wrong group** — IAM group membership issue. Verify with HR/IT.
3. **All denies on one app** — Rule may be misconfigured. Review policy.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **No private access events** — Harmony Connect client may not be deployed.
• **All traffic showing Accept** — Private Access policy may be in permissive mode.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Check Point App for Splunk (Splunkbase 4293)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cp_log into zt. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`dst, fail_pct, ok, rule_name`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Check Point's private access lets employees reach internal applications without a VPN. We track who can connect, who gets blocked, and why — so we can fix the problems that keep people from their work while still maintaining strict access controls.
hardware: Check Point Harmony SASE (cloud), Harmony Connect Client, Harmony SASE Connector (on-prem)
